items.item: Each row shows the user's name and email, role, status in words (such as Active, Invited, Deactivated, Locked) and whether two-factor sign-in is enabled
items.evidence: rowHtml() (page.html:497-519) renders name, email, role badge and statusBadge() text (Active/Invited/Deactivated only, no 'Locked' state in DATA or statusBadge config). No two-factor/2FA column or indicator exists anywhere in rowHtml, buildMenuItems, or DATA objects.

items.item: Last sign-in uses one date-time format with the timezone stated, relative times also expose the exact time, and an account that has never signed in shows "Never" rather than a blank or a 1970 date
items.evidence: timeAgo() returns 'Never' for null lastSignIn (good), and the relative text has a title tooltip from formatExact() (page.html:419-423, 513). But formatExact() uses d.toLocaleString(undefined,{dateStyle:'medium',timeStyle:'short'}) with no timezone abbreviation/offset shown anywhere, so the 'timezone stated' requirement fails.

items.item: Users can be found by searching name or email and filtered by role, status and inactivity (such as no sign-in for 90+ days), with the number of matching users shown
items.evidence: searchInput filters name/email and #roleFilter/#statusFilter filter role and status (page.html:945-954); #resultsCount shows 'N users' (line 193, 579). There is no inactivity/90+ days filter control anywhere in the markup or getFiltered() logic (page.html:462-484).

items.item: The invite form requires an email and a role, labels both fields, and shows an inline error for a malformed address or one that already has an account
items.evidence: inviteEmail and inviteRole are both required with associated <label> elements (page.html:294-304); submit handler validates with emailRe and checks DATA.some(...) for an existing account, showing text in #inviteEmailError with role="alert" (page.html:992-1006).

items.item: Deactivation asks for confirmation that names the user and states the effect (active sessions ended, sign-in blocked, data kept), and a deactivated user is offered Reactivate instead
items.evidence: Confirm dialog text is only "<name> will immediately lose access to the workspace. You can reactivate this account at any time." (page.html:760) — it names the user and mentions reactivation, but never states that active sessions are ended, sign-in is blocked, or that data is kept. Reactivate option for deactivated users does exist via buildMenuItems() deactivateLabel/action (page.html:522-523).

items.item: The signed-in administrator's own row is marked (such as "You") and cannot be deactivated or lose the admin role, and the last remaining administrator cannot be deactivated, with the disabled action explaining why
items.evidence: The signed-in admin, Jordan Diaz (jordan.diaz@acmecorp.com, shown in sidebar/topbar, page.html:65,96-97), does not appear anywhere in the DATA array (page.html:351-367) or table, so no row is marked 'You'. buildMenuItems() only disables deactivate for role==='Owner' (ownerLocked, page.html:524,531); there is no 'last remaining admin' check and no protection tied to the signed-in user at all.

items.item: Password reset sends a reset link to the user's email address, which the confirmation names, and the administrator never sees, sets or types the new password
items.evidence: Confirm dialog: "Send a password reset link to " + user.email + "?" and on confirm toast "Password reset link sent to " + user.email + "." (page.html:749-755); no password input field exists anywhere in the UI.

items.item: Row actions are buttons or a keyboard-operable menu whose accessible names include the user (such as "Actions for Mai Nguyen"), and the outcome of an action is announced in an aria-live or role="status" region
items.evidence: menu-trigger button: aria-label="Actions for " + escapeHtml(u.name) (page.html:515), matching the example pattern; menu items are real <button role="menuitem"> elements (buildMenuItems, page.html:521-535) reachable/activatable by keyboard. Outcomes are announced via #toastContainer which has aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true" (page.html:343) and toast() messages like "...account has been deactivated." (page.html:766).

items.item: A search with no matching users shows a message with a way to clear it, and loading and failed-load states with a retry exist
items.evidence: #emptyState shows "No users found" / "Try adjusting your search or filters." plus a "Clear filters" button wired to #clearFilters (page.html:246-251, 955-964) — satisfies the no-results half. However there is no loading state (spinner/skeleton) and no failed-load/error state with a retry button anywhere in the markup or script; data renders synchronously from a static in-memory array (DATA, page.html:350-367).

notes: Stat cards (Total users / Active / Pending invites / Deactivated) are classic icon+number KPI tiles with no trend context, flagged by the audit as rounded-xl (12px) exceeding the 8px radius-scale cap. Sidebar is bg-slate-900 navy with indigo-600 accents on the logo mark, active-state elements, and primary buttons. Audit also flags real defects worth noting: plain-text emails should be mailto: links (contact-link, 8 occurrences), card shadows should be borders only (surface-shadow), and all 8 visible rows are two-line/65px exceeding the two-line row-height cap (table-row-height / table-row-two-line).
